title: Speaking to Her Heart
note: Overwhelmed and with nothing to hold on to, she speaks to her heart, not knowing what to do. This comes once her features have lost their beauty, so it follows that chapter.

couplets.plain: Won’t you think of something, heart, and tell me any cure at all for this unending sickness?
couplets.pm: My heart, I haven’t the power to find it. Whatever it may be, find out and tell me one medicine for this sickness that nothing relieves. “Any at all” means even something that gives up modesty, which is worth more than life.
couplets.context: She asks how her suffering might be ended.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Won’t you think of something, heart

links.reason: Her suffering is a sickness that won’t end, and she goes looking for a cure anyway.

couplets.plain: He has no love for you, yet you go on suffering. That is foolishness, my heart, long may you live.
couplets.pm: He has no love for us, yet you suffer, waiting for him to come. That is your own foolishness and nothing else. He doesn’t think of us, so we can tell he has no love, and you don’t see that. You don’t think of going to him either, and you bring this on yourself. “Long may you live” is mockery. The wise thing is for us to go to him.
couplets.context: Her longing to see him overwhelms her, and she says this.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: my heart, long may you live
links.reason: Scolds the heart to its face, closing on a mocking blessing.

links.quote: He has no love for you, yet you go on suffering

couplets.plain: Why sit here thinking of him and aching, heart? The one who gave us this sickness of grief has no tender thought for us.
couplets.pm: My heart, you neither go to him nor die here. Why sit thinking of his return and suffering? The man who gave us this sickness of grief won’t think of us with pity and come. He has no compassion for us, so he won’t come of himself. It is right now that we go to him.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Why sit here thinking of him and aching
links.reason: Asks what good it does to sit aching for a man who has no tender thought for her.

links.quote: Why sit here thinking of him and aching, heart?
links.reason: Speaks to the heart as a partner in a useless vigil she now wants to end.

links.quote: has no tender thought for us
links.reason: A plain argument for anyone stuck: the one who gave you this sickness has no tender thought for you.

couplets.plain: Take my eyes with you too when you go, heart. Wanting to see him, they are eating me.
couplets.pm: My heart, if you go to him, take these eyes with you. If you go without them, their craving will torment me as if devouring me, demanding that I show him to them. She wants that torment ended, which means she herself intends to go.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Take my eyes with you too when you go, heart
Wanting to see him, they are eating me

couplets.plain: We are drawn to him and he isn’t drawn to us. Can we give him up as an enemy, heart?
couplets.pm: He doesn’t return the loving-kindness we give him. Do we have the strength to decide he hates us, sulk and give him up? We don’t. Since we lack that strength, the right thing for us is to go to him.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: treats clinging to someone who spurns you as the only course

links.quote: Can we give him up as an enemy, heart?

couplets.plain: When you see the lover who mends a sulk with an embrace, you can’t even sulk. Your anger now is a pretence, my heart.
couplets.pm: If I sulk, my lover can end it by making love. When you see him, you can’t sulk even once in pretence and then give it up. You can’t do that, yet now you rage at him as cruel. That is false anger with no firmness in it. If you fail when you see him, hating him when you don’t is useless. Stop, and make up your mind to go to him.
couplets.context: Her heart thinks of his cruelty and won’t agree to go. She scolds it.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Your anger now is a pretence, my heart

couplets.plain: Good heart, give up desire or give up modesty. I can’t bear them both.
couplets.pm: Good heart, if you won’t give up modesty, give up desire. If you won’t give up that, give up modesty. If you mean to keep both, I haven’t the strength to carry two opposites at once, even if you have. She calls the heart good because keeping both preserves a woman’s womanhood. That is good, but her life can’t stand it.
couplets.context: Her modesty holds her back, so she gives up going, and she says this.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: give up desire or give up modesty

couplets.plain: You pine because he won’t show tender kindness, and you go after the one who left. You are a fool, my heart.
couplets.pm: My heart, you think he shows no kindness only because he doesn’t know how I suffer, and you would go pining after him to tell him. You know nothing. He saw my suffering and left without kindness. It is foolish to think he will come just because you told him, away from the sight of it.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: you go after the one who left
links.reason: By mocking the heart for going after a man who left, she sides with holding back.

links.quote: You are a fool, my heart.
you go after the one who left
links.reason: Tells anyone tempted to go after someone who left that pining and pursuit are a fool’s way.

couplets.plain: Your lover is within you, my heart. Whom are you thinking of, and to whom are you going?
couplets.pm: My heart, your lover is inside you. You have seen it all before, so who is it you go searching for outside? To go looking outside for someone who lives within you, not knowing it, is laughable. Give it up.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her heart.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Your lover is within you, my heart.

couplets.plain: If we keep in our heart the one who left us and won’t come near, we will lose still more of our beauty.
couplets.pm: He left us so that we can’t be together. If we keep him within us, we will lose the inner beauty that remains as well as the outer beauty already gone. He has left and won’t come near us, and we can’t forget him, so we will lose even the composure we still have.
couplets.context: She says this to mean that she must forget him and bear it.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty
If we keep in our heart the one who left us
links.reason: States the cost outright: keeping someone who left in your heart costs you more of your beauty.

ideaLinks.quote: give up desire or give up modesty
ideaLinks.reason: She tells her heart that desire and modesty can’t both be borne: one has to go.
